question: Assume today is 2026-08-25. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of births in Japan in July 2026, as first reported in the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's preliminary monthly vital statistics (which also count foreign nationals in Japan).

target.what: Number of live births occurring in Japan during July 2026, as counted in the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's preliminary monthly vital statistics (人口動態統計速報), which includes foreign nationals resident in Japan
target.publisher: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (厚生労働省), preliminary monthly vital statistics (人口動態統計速報)
target.cadence: monthly, published roughly two months after the reference month (July 2026 preliminary typically released around early September 2026)
target.caveats: Target period is completed but the official preliminary figure is not yet published at the 2026-08-25 cutoff, so the estimate must be built from prior months' preliminary counts, seasonal patterns, and related series. Definitional notes: preliminary monthly vital statistics count births occurring in

candidates.perspective: MHLW preliminary monthly vital statistics time series
candidates.hypothesis: July 2026 births will follow the level and seasonal pattern of July preliminary counts in recent years, adjusted for the ongoing downward trend; the same-month prior-year values and the most recent 2025-2026 monthly preliminary values anchor the level.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly preliminary birth counts (速報) for Japan for each month from 2019 through June 2026, especially July values for 2019-2025 and the latest available months (Jan-Jun 2026); also year-on-year ratios for July in each year.

assumptions.applies_when: July 2026 behaves like the recent 2026 monthly pattern relative to the same month a year earlier.
assumptions.falsified_by: A June 2026 preliminary release showing a sharp deviation from the May/Jan-May pattern.

kept.rationale: Recent preliminary data show near-flat YoY: Jan-May 2026 cumulative +0.4% (p6/p7), trailing-12m -0.4% (p10/p11), May 2026 -1.7% (p1/p2), Jan-Feb 2026 +0.1% (p139/p140). July 2025 was already low; a small decline to flat is the central case, with wide tails for monthly noise.
kept.applies_when: July 2026 behaves like the recent Jan-May 2026 pattern of near-flat YoY change.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp July-specific drop or rebound (e.g., a June 2026 preliminary showing a large YoY swing).

kept.name: July share of annual all-resident births
kept.rationale: July 2025 62,521 / 2025 all-resident 694,162 (p43/p104) is about 0.090; July 2024 64,283 / 2024 717,291 (p44/p41) is about 0.0896. July is a high-birth month; share is stable around 0.086-0.090.
kept.applies_when: July's seasonal share of annual births remains near its 2024-2025 level.
kept.falsified_by: A marked shift in the July seasonal pattern.

kept.name: 2026 annual all-resident births relative to 2025 all-resident births
kept.rationale: 2025 all-resident births were 694,162 (p104). Recent YoY is near-flat (p6/p7, p10/p11), so 2026 is expected within a few percent of 2025; central case a small decline.
kept.applies_when: 2026 annual births continue the recent near-flat trend relative to 2025.
kept.falsified_by: A published 2026 annual projection far outside this range.

kept.name: July 2026 vs July 2025 change factor for Japanese-population births
kept.rationale: Japanese-population July births fell 64,034 (2023) to 62,304 (2024) to 60,647 (2025), about -2.7% then -2.7%; the recent national preliminary trend is near-flat, so a small decline is the central case.
kept.applies_when: Japanese-population July births continue their recent gentle decline.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp July-specific drop or rebound in Japanese-population births.

kept.name: Foreign-resident share of July births
kept.rationale: July 2025 foreign 1,874 / all-resident 62,521 (p34/p43) is about 0.030; July 2024 1,979/64,283 (p35/p44) is about 0.031; July 2023 1,586/65,620 (p127/p109) is about 0.024. Share is stable near 3%.
kept.applies_when: Foreign-resident share of July births stays near 3%.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp change in foreign-resident births.

The best computed estimate for live births occurring in Japan during July 2026, as counted in the MHLW preliminary monthly vital statistics (all residents, including foreign nationals), is 61,597 person (80% model-based interval 44,711 to 84,860 person).

Two methods were combined with weights 50% and 50%. The first anchors on the observed July 2025 all-resident count of 62,521 births and applies a near-flat year-on-year factor of 0.985 (range 0.8801 to 1.1). The second builds from the observed July 2025 Japanese-population count of 60,647 births, a factor of 0.985 (range 0.8801 to 1.1), and a foreign-resident share of 0.03 (range 0.02107 to 0.04214).

Only the July 2025 levels and the foreign share are observed; the change factors and share stability are assumptions. The main risk is that July 2026 deviates from the near-flat trend. The most useful missing evidence is the actual July 2026 preliminary count, unavailable at the cutoff.

- a1 July 2026 vs July 2025 all-resident birth change factor: 0.985 ratio, range 0.8801 to 1.1 (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence of a sharp July-specific drop or rebound (e.g., a June 2026 preliminary showing a large YoY swing).
- a4 July 2026 vs July 2025 change factor for Japanese-population births: 0.985 ratio, range 0.8801 to 1.1 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence of a sharp July-specific drop or rebound in Japanese-population births.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
